clue.text: Hard having up to a stone to lift — but this stone's much heavier!

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the pieces means reading them upwards, so the whole chain runs backwards

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
till (shortened to til) means up to
a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A heavy stone must be lifted, but the next one is a far greater burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lift' reverses the whole run H + TIL + A + GEM. The definition plays on the gem: this stone is far heavier than a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: A megalith is a huge standing stone, vastly heavier than a gemstone.

clue.text: Motor manufacturer taking short curve before angled chicane?

indicators.note: short means the word for curve loses its last letter

parts.note: a bend is a curve in a road
the letter Z has the zigzag shape of a chicane on a racetrack

explanation.surface: A car maker's driver takes a quick bend before a sharp chicane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims BEND to BEN. Z is pictured as the shape of an angled chicane.
explanation.definitionFit: Benz (Mercedes-Benz) is a German car maker.

clue.text: Somewhat tipsy (cheeky, mind)

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being a little drunk makes one cheeky, mind you.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind in psychology.

clue.text: Slight cut, then hip given hormonal injection

indicators.note: cut means the word for slight loses its final letter

parts.note: a slight is an insult
in means fashionable, as hip does

explanation.surface: A small nick, then a hip jab with a hormone shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective but is the noun meaning an insult; 'cut' trims INSULT to INSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone that diabetics take by injection.

clue.text: Strong position taken over wife accessing flexible toy, as Adams' comprehensive solution

parts.note: a fort is a fortified, strong position

indicators.note: accessing means the letter for wife gets inside the scrambled toy letters
flexible means the letters of toy bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A fortress whose wife gets at a bendy toy somehow sums up the universe, per Adams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' rearranges TOY to YTO, and 'accessing' puts W inside to make YTWO. In Douglas Adams' Hitchhiker's Guide, 42 is the answer to life, the universe and everything.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy the computer gives 42 as the ultimate answer to everything.

clue.text: As a ship runs out of cargo, none, I suspect, good

indicators.note: I suspect signals that the letters are a guess at a new order
out of means the letter for runs is taken away from cargo

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A ship sails without any cargo, which one suspects is good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' does double duty in look only: I is fodder and 'suspect' the anagram signal. 'out of' removes R from CARGO, giving CAGO; CAGO + NONE + I is rearranged to OCEANGOIN, then G.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean-going vessel is a ship built for the open sea, so it describes a ship.

clue.text: Russian transport where unpleasant type secreted in craft turned up

indicators.note: secreted in means the unpleasant type is hidden within the word for craft
in a down clue turned up means the word for craft is read upwards

parts.note: art is skill or craft
oik is British slang for a boorish, unpleasant person

explanation.surface: A Russian vehicle in which a lout has been smuggled inside an upturned boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a boat, but here it means skill. OIK is a British insult for a lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian carriage or sleigh drawn by three horses abreast.

clue.text: See 9
Man of 10 soon improvised around layers?

indicators.note: around means the reordered letters sit on either side of the layers
improvised means the letters of soon are played freely into a new order

parts.note: carpeters are those who lay carpets, cryptically layers

explanation.surface: A jazz man would soon be improvising around other layers of sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks like strata of sound but means people who lay carpets. 10 is JAZZ, so the man is a jazz musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Peterson was a celebrated Canadian jazz pianist, a man of jazz.

clue.text: Irregular notes, given European agreement, sound in the House of Lords?

parts.note: ja is the German word for yes

parts.words: sound in the House of Lords
parts.note: zz is the cartoon sound of snoring, as by dozing peers in the House of Lords

explanation.surface: Peculiar notes, agreed by Europe, are sounded in the upper chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: The House of Lords is Britain's upper parliamentary chamber, whose elderly members are joked to sleep through debates.
explanation.definitionFit: Jazz is music built on syncopated, irregular rhythms and improvised notes.

clue.text: Consider one in essence, man of 10

parts.note: to count is to consider or regard

indicators.note: in means the numeral one goes inside the word for essence

parts.note: the base is the essential foundation of something
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Thinking of a single person at heart, a man of jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Count Basie was an American jazz pianist and bandleader.

clue.text: Lady of 10 finds party backing politician's promise before recess

indicators.note: backing means the party's letters are read backwards

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
a lie, as a cynic sees a politician's promise
a parliamentary recess is a holiday

explanation.surface: A lady finds her party turning on a politician's vow just before the summer recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns LIB into BIL. Billie Holiday was nicknamed Lady Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Billie Holiday, known as Lady Day, was a great jazz singer.

clue.text: Vocal hindrance styling air roughly?

indicators.note: roughly means the letters are handled loosely and rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer's hairdresser roughly styling the air may be hampering the voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Laryngitis is inflammation of the voice box that makes speaking hard.

clue.text: Function whose differential may be altering

indicators.note: a differential is a difference, so the word that follows may be a different arrangement

explanation.surface: A calculus function whose derivative might keep changing.
explanation.walkthrough: In calculus an integral is the function whose differential is a given one, so the surface reads as maths; 'differential' signals the rearranging of ALTERING.
explanation.definitionFit: In calculus an integral is a function obtained by integration.

clue.text: Man of 10, Wally, given coat, say

parts.note: wally and charlie are both British slang for a fool

indicators.note: say signals that the coat is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a parka is a hooded coat

explanation.surface: A jazz man, a bit of a fool, is handed a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLY and CHARLIE are British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Parker was a jazz saxophonist, a founder of bebop.

clue.text: What did I do in restaurant? Start

parts.note: taken as written
the restaurant is referred to as it, as in 'in it'
what did I do: I ate, the answer to the question

explanation.surface: Asked what one did at the restaurant, the reply begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Answer the question 'What did I do in restaurant?': in it, I ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to start or begin something.

clue.text: See 12
Expecting a fly to tour small island

indicators.note: to tour means to go round, so the words for a and fly surround the island

parts.note: to wing is to fly
an ait is a small river island

explanation.surface: Anticipating a flight round a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: An ait (or eyot) is a small island in a river such as the Thames; 'fly' is the verb, not the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Awaiting means waiting for, or expecting, something.

clue.text: Boring claiming black magic is what it is?

indicators.note: claiming means the word for boring takes the other word inside it

parts.note: dry means dull and boring
black magic is evil

explanation.surface: A dull chap insists that the occult is what it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what it is' refers back to black magic: it is evil.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry is wicked mischief, especially black magic or sorcery.

clue.text: Cosy before this order of battle?

definitions.meaning: one sits cosily in front of a fire in an open hearth
the command to troops to start shooting

explanation.definitionFit: An open hearth fire is a cosy thing to sit before, and the phrase is also a battle command.

clue.text: See 15
State male's attached to rug for house on reservation

parts.note: rug is slang for a wig
WA is the abbreviation for Washington State
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A state man is attached to a rug for his dwelling on the reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigwam is a domed dwelling of Native Americans, who live on reservations.

clue.text: See 24 across
Fake left behind lorry: if pinched, one heading for auction

indicators.note: pinched means the word if is squeezed inside the lorry

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A fake truck left behind, nicked if possible, for auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places L last. ARTIC is a British articulated lorry (a semi-trailer truck).
explanation.definitionFit: Artificial means fake, not natural or genuine.

clue.text: After broadcast, small screen captured man of 10

indicators.note: captured means the scrambled letters hold the other pieces inside
broadcast means the letters of after are scattered into a new order

parts.note: a wall is a screen or barrier

explanation.surface: After a broadcast, a small screen caught a jazz man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns AFTER into FATER before the small screen goes inside it; 'After' looks like a time word but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Waller was a jazz pianist and composer.

clue.text: Material tested for texture

definitions.meaning: a cloth made of matted wool fibres
touched to judge how something feels

explanation.definitionFit: Felt is a pressed woollen fabric and the past tense of feel, touching to sense texture.

clue.text: Be old before one's time

parts.note: ex means former or old
one's is I'S, I being one

explanation.surface: Being former before one's time.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is simply to be, to have being.

clue.text: Wine right, that is, to chuck

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is
to sling is to chuck or throw

explanation.surface: This wine is just right, that is, for throwing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a white grape and the wine made from it.
